name: real-app-hls
_comment: FrameConsole's browser viewing path (HLS, run with --host <sender IP>, 127.0.0.1 when the generator runs on the sender PC). Every viewer is a Node LL-HLS client: POST /screen-01/session (+ PUT heartbeat, DELETE on leave, as the page), live.m3u8, the variant of its quality, init, parts with blocking reloads, video + AAC. Quality per plan: source only here; a mix with --qualities source=0.7,720p=0.3 (the app must offer 720p). Stages 1-10-50-100-300-500-1000, hold 45 s each; on one PC the stop rules (generator threads, host CPU/memory, success, 429/503 share, degraded rate) end the run long before 1000 - that is a loopback limit, never 1,000 internet viewers. Target statistics only from the app's read-only GET /api/stats (v 1): ingest per path as the full-rate reference, hls.sessions as the target session count, http.refused. The app answers Connection: close and counts every HLS request in its 400 in-flight slots (http_server.cpp kMaxRequests), so 503 Busy answers are expected past a few hundred LL-HLS viewers. One headless Edge page with the real UI (hls.js) runs in a separate phase after the holds of stages 1 and 10: decoded fps and real delay, kept apart from the media-load numbers. Traffic cap 200 GB is loopback/LAN protection only; lower it with --max-traffic-gb on any metered link.
